newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-STIMPSON KICKS LIONS TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-STIMPSON KICKS LIONS TO VICTORY.

text.p: Fullback Tim Stimpson steered the British Lions to a third successive victory on their South African tour with a near faultless kicking display against Western Province on Saturday.
Stimpson was successful with seven out of eight kicks at goal for a total of 18 points as the Lions again had to come from behind in the second half to secure a 38-21 win.
A second try for wing John Bentley in the final move of the match flattered the Lions who had struggled to establish forward dominance.
They were regularly shunted backwards on their own feed at the scrums, although their backs again proved they have firepower out wide by scoring all four of their tries.

Ignited by flyhalf Gregor Townsend, they again began explosively with the Scotsman's jink towards the posts creating the confusion for centre Jeremy Guscott to make room for Bentley to jog over in the left-hand corner.

Two Stimpson penalties either side of the try gave the Lions a 13-0 lead midway through the opening half but Western Province captain and centre Dick Muir dummied down the blindside of a ruck on the Lions' tryline to score the first of his two tries.

The home side opted for scrums when awarded penalties near the Lions' line and their ability to disrupt the touring team's scrum paid off four minutes before the interval when Muir again went down the blindside after Province had pinned the Lions on their own line.
In between Muir's tries slick passing between centre Allan Tait, Guscott and Bentley had led to a try for Tait which ensured the Lions held a narrow 18-14 lead at the interval.
Flanker Robby Brink scored a try under the posts, converted by flyhalf Percival Montgomery, to make it 21-18 to the home side eight minutes into the new half.
But two more Stimpson penalties nosed the Lions back ahead before two tries from broken play sealed their win.
Scrumhalf Rob Howley knifed through a disorganised Province defence from halfway, gaining 30 metres to make the opening for winger Ieuan Evans to go over in the corner.
With time running out Bentley -- who had twice had to be separated from needling opposite number and Springbok wing James Small -- picked up a loose ball to jog over in the corner.
Stimpson, from the left-hand touchline, sealed a fine afternoon's kicking, by thumping the conversion through the posts.

Western Province - 15-Justin Swart, 14-James Small, 13-Robbie Fleck, 12-Dick Muir (captain), 11-Simon Berridge, 10-Percival Montgomery, 9-Stephen Hatley, 8-Andrew Aitken, 7-Corne Krige (Bobby Skinstad, 64), 6-Robby Brink, 5-Hottie Louw, 4-Fritz van Herden, 3-Keith Andrews, 2-Andrew Paterson, 1-Garry Pagel (Toks van der Linde, 56).

British Lions - 15-Tim Stimpson, 14-John Bentley, 13-Jeremy Guscott, 12-Allan Tait (Will Greenwood, 72), 11-Ieuan Evans, 10-Gregor Townsend, 9-Rob Howley, 8-Tim Rodber (Scott Quinnell, 63), 7-Richard Hill, 6-Lawrence Dallaglio, 5-Simon Shaw, 4-Martin Johnson (captain), 3-Jason Leonard, 2-Barry Williams, 1-Graham Rowntree.
